dedupe_keys.name: space weather canada forecasts and geomagnetic ionospheric and solar data

description: Space Weather Canada, run by Natural Resources Canada, gives information on space weather conditions, data and services. It offers current geomagnetic activity, a review and forecast from the observatories, current conditions with short and long term forecasts, and a data and plots section with geomagnetic, ionospheric and solar data. Other sections explain space weather effects on satellites, radio systems and ground networks, and give information, data and plots from the Canadian magnetic observatories. Access is free and public on a Government of Canada site; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: the home page was last modified in 2019, and the data pages are organised by product, so formats and periods vary. Coverage is Canada. It supports hazard exposure and emergency response analysis of geomagnetic storms for power grids, pipelines, satellites and radio communications; related records are the NRCan space weather effects chronology and the Hydro-Québec March 1989 blackout case study.
